### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **43** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/system/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**59** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ff6f9768d2969c4f2f42819f461424965238e30f`.

⛔ **17** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/system/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `isSystem (5 routes)`
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **189** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ff6f9768d2969c4f2f42819f461424965238e30f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9fc252d3b42e5188c4310a693e07ea4ca01e115e` — the merge of head `98cbc476025ff17adedde53e62f0cb8bcdbba110` into base `ff6f9768d2969c4f2f42819f461424965238e30f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9fc252d3b42e5188c4310a693e07ea4ca01e115e && git checkout 9fc252d3b42e5188c4310a693e07ea4ca01e115e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ff6f9768d2969c4f2f42819f461424965238e30f 98cbc476025ff17adedde53e62f0cb8bcdbba110 && git checkout -B drift-repro ff6f9768d2969c4f2f42819f461424965238e30f && git merge --no-ff 98cbc476025ff17adedde53e62f0cb8bcdbba110

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ff6f9768d2969c4f2f42819f461424965238e30f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ff6f9768d2969c4f2f42819f461424965238e30f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `03e453e3d3076da4777dd5c288232b81561ce9a2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts + packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-standard-unit-setting.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-standard-unit-setting.object.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/system/index.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/plugin.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/setup-nav.contributions.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/default-permission-sets.standard-unit-setting.integration.test.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts, packages/cli/test/connect-agent-both-halves-wire.pin.test.ts, scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.json, .changeset/35498-standard-unit-setting.md (translation bundles spot-checked: zh-CN objects, de hashes, the eleven nav labels, bundle-ownership.test.ts)
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

### ① Derived judgments

Read: card #35498 (body, every comment; amendments 7178077326, 7178144166, 7179529249), ruling record 7008551416 on #35339, ADR-0158 (U3, U6, L4, Open item 10) on `main`, the ADR row 7179515770 on #37245, the PR body, the net diff, and the check-runs on the head (every run `success` or `skipped`; on the names that ran twice, `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` are `success` on the newer run, `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size` are `skipped` on the newer run; `Test Core`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness` all `success`).

- **`PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['platform-objects']` gains `sys_standard_unit_setting`** (the one `hits` path). Right: add-only, in sort order, and it is what the reference lints and the catalog read, so the name becomes a reference target a nav entry or lookup may name. A widening of the public surface, nothing removed or re-meant.
- **New platform object, accept set.** `code` text, max 3, admitted by an anchored, case-sensitive pattern built from `Object.keys(STANDARD_UNITS)`; `decimal_places` required, 0..`UNIT_DECIMAL_PLACES_MAX` (12), scale 0; unique `code` per organization; `code` immutable by an update-only `cross_field` rule in the same `previous != null && …` spelling `sys_unit` uses. Right against the precedent (`sys_unit.decimal_places`: same range, same constant, imported not re-spelled) and against L4 (a display default, nothing rounds at write; nothing in the diff touches a record write). The pattern is derived from the table, so a code U1 gains is admitted with no second edit: right.
- **`code` as text plus a format rule, not a select.** Right, and declared (7179529249): a select would store `kgm`, U4 stores the code in exact uppercase. The unit test refuses `kgm`, `Kgm`, `C62`, `EA`, an org code, `KGMX`, a padded code and the empty string; the integration suite refuses `BOX_12`, `kgm`, `EA` at 400 on `code`.
- **Clear = delete; `decimal_places` required.** Right as declared (7178144166, superseding 7178077326). The API serves delete (no `apiMethods` whitelist, unlike `sys_unit`); a deleted row frees nothing a stored record depends on, since the code stays standard. This is where the object deliberately leaves the `sys_unit` precedent, and the reason holds.
- **`member_default`: read only, no write bit, no row policy.** Right for least privilege: the card's Done-when asks exactly this ("a member can read them"), the line carries all three write bits `false`, and an explicit line is the set's whole answer for its object. Pinned: member list returns exactly `[['GRM', 3]]`; member create, edit and delete are each 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` with the stored row unchanged; the PR's ablation (`allowRead: false`) reddens the member-read and cross-organization-read tests.
- **`organization_admin`: explicit line, create/edit/delete, no superuser bits.** Right, and it is a narrowing of what the set's `'*'` line would otherwise give (the wildcard carries `viewAllRecords`, `modifyAllRecords`, `viewAllFields`); the derived no-bypass variant inherits the line. Read against the code: `effectiveSharingModel` resolves an unset model on a platform object to public, and the owner-only floor is bound to `org_member`, so an administrator reaches every setting of the organization without the bits. Pinned for the creator's own rows only: see S2.
- **`external_default`: no line.** Right as read (the set has no wildcard and no `sys_standard_unit_setting` entry, so the object is denied). Not pinned: N2.
- **Tenancy: no opt-out, `organization_id` injected, census `in` reach, inventory `attribution` with no anchors, same citation as `sys_unit`.** Right. Census totals move 110→111 registered and 59→60 in reach, `outOfReach` unchanged: consistent.
- **Cross-organization isolation.** Right under the `isolated` posture, with real positive controls: both organizations hold a `GRM` row (which also proves the unique key is per organization, not installation-wide); a member and an administrator see neither the other row by list nor by id; an update and a delete aimed at the other row leave it byte-for-byte as stored. The wall is a posture property, not a property of this object: S1.
- **Organization delete.** Right as pinned: 409 `DELETE_RESTRICTED`, `dependentObject` = this object, the organization still stored; then success once the row is deleted.
- **Setup nav entry, no `requiredPermissions`.** Right: same reasoning as `nav_units_of_measure` directly above it (the object grant decides, Setup itself needs `setup.access`); the count pin moves 36→37 and names the entry; the unit test pins position and target view.
- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)`.** Right: a new object, two new grant lines, a new registry name and a new nav entry; nothing existing is refused or re-meant. Same declaration as `sys_unit`'s own changeset (`35488-standard-unit-table-sys-unit.md`).
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`.** Right: no key, accepted value, or metadata type an author writes is added, removed or re-meant; the object is organization runtime data. The registry name is a reference target, not a protocol key; `sys_unit` joined the same list under `none`, and the unit key itself (`unitConfig`, #35489) is where `added` was declared.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/cli` — right: each package has a source change, and AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 gives a non-protocol widening `patch`. Both declaration lines are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset and agree. `Check Changeset` is `success` on its newer run.

Changeset, sentence by sentence:
- Lead paragraph (admin sets per-code display decimals; one row per code; 0 to 12; delete clears; org units keep theirs on `sys_unit`): true.
- "Every member reads … organization administrators and owners create, edit and delete … External members get no read": true (owner pinned; external read by reading only, N2).
S1 (should-fix) — "`organization_id` is injected, so the tenant wall scopes every read and write; another organization's setting is never read" is stated without its condition, and is not true in every posture. ADR-0105 D1: `single` (the default) has no wall between organizations and no stamping; `group` walls by `organization_id IN accessible_org_ids`, so a person in two organizations reads both. The PR body's own acceptance note says the same ("Under the default `single` posture no tenant wall stands, so another organization's row is visible"). The behaviour is the platform's and is right; the shipped CHANGELOG sentence overclaims an isolation guarantee. Say it as it is: "where a tenant wall stands (`isolated`; `group` by membership), `organization_id` is stamped and the wall scopes every read and write". The same unconditional wording sits in the object's `Tenancy` docblock and the `member_default` comment, where it copies `sys_unit`'s; fix the changeset, the comments may follow. I weighed this as must-fix (a false security sentence in a published file) and held it at should-fix because the code is correct, the precedent's wording is the same, and the changeset can still be corrected before the release PR consumes it.
- "Every set, change and clear is written to `sys_audit_log`, with field history on both columns": true where plugin-audit is mounted; pinned with old and new values and `tenant_id`.
N1 (nit) — "No reader ships in this change; the quantity display reads it": the second half is present tense for something that does not exist on this head. "The quantity display (#35490) will read it."
- "Like an exchange rate … refused (`DELETE_RESTRICTED`) until its settings are deleted": true for this object as pinned; the exchange-rate half is read from the area's amendment, not re-derived here.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations (os-dev-report 7179477079), each answered:
- Clear = delete: accepted, area amendment 7178144166; pinned.
- `code` text plus format rule: accepted, 7179529249; pinned.
- One file beyond the confirmed surface (`connect-agent-both-halves-wire.pin.test.ts`): accepted, 7179529249; it is a count pin the new entry moves, nothing else in the file changes.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)`: right, ① above.
- `Refs` then `Fixes #35498`: the PR body now says `Fixes`. Two of the card's Done-when lines are not true at merge: "Display (#35490) reads the setting" (deferred to #35490 by 7178077326) and "ADR-0158 records the answer" (row 7179515770 on #37245, unchecked, ordered after this merge). Both are tracked and the area accepted the close (7179529249).
N4 (nit) — between this merge and the weekly ADR card, ADR-0158 on `main` still reads "have no home: Open item 10" and "a ruling is owed. Not settled here" while the tree and its docblocks cite Open item 10 as answered; the seat should not let row 7179515770 slip a week.
- Commit trailer pair: no contract effect.

`open_questions`: empty. `security_findings: none` from the dev: I agree on the code; S1 is a wording finding and S2 a missing pin.

Out-of-scope finding the dev reported (`pnpm check:platform-checklist` red on `main` for `FlowItemMoreMenu.tsx#FlowItemMoreMenu` in `areas/automation.json`): not this diff; escalated to the seat to file or dedupe.

`packages/spec/scripts/lib/platform-catalog.ts` is on the amended file surface and is not in the diff. Right for now: the catalog is the app-facing subset with a "how the app reaches it" column, and nothing reaches this object until the reader ships. #35490 owes the row, or a decision that it stays out.

For #35490 (the reader), from this read: it must pick the row by the record's or the active organization, not "the row for the code". Under `group` a reader can see more than one organization's row for one code, and under `single` rows are unstamped. The L4 clamp to the field's `scale` is also still owed there; a stored 12 is legal here by design.

SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no query, id materialisation or in-app join is added; the uniqueness is a declared index and the isolation is Layer 0's predicate. Nothing to find.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts` — holds. One add-only name, registered by the package the map says owns it (`com.objectstack.platform-objects`, first manifest, beside `sys_unit`); the unit test pins the membership and the registering manifest.

Implementing files against the contract (ruling 7008551416: an organization admin may set the display decimals of any standard U1 code, in a new organization-owned setting place; L4 unchanged):
- `sys-standard-unit-setting.object.ts` — agrees. Any U1 code, only U1 codes, organization-owned, a display default with no write-time effect. The settings-key route was measured and not followed for stated reasons (one org-wide scalar, projection-only member read, hash-only audit); the `sys_*` route gives per-code rows, value audit and a member read grant, which is what the card's Done-when asks.
- `default-permission-sets.ts` — agrees, least privilege on both lines.
S2 (should-fix) — the `organization_admin` comment claims "an administrator edits every setting of their organization without [the superuser bits]", and nothing pins it. In the suite each of `carol` and `owen` sets, changes and clears only a row they created themselves. The `sys_unit` suite pins exactly this for edit (`default-permission-sets.unit-of-measure.integration.test.ts`, "an administrator edits every unit of the organization, not only their own"), and here the line also carries delete, which `sys_unit`'s does not, so the delete half has no precedent pin at all. By reading it holds (public OWD on a platform object; the `owner_only_writes` / `owner_only_deletes` floor binds `org_member`), but a line that deliberately drops `modifyAllRecords` should carry the pin: the owner changes and clears a setting the administrator created.
N2 (nit) — "External members get no read" is asserted in the changeset, the PR body and the `member_default` comment and exercised by no persona in the suite.
N3 (nit) — the cross-organization write test swallows both outcomes (a bare `.catch` returning nothing) and asserts stored state only. Enough for isolation; it leaves unpinned whether the caller meets a refusal or a silent no-op.
N5 (nit) — `nav_standard_unit_settings` reuses the `ruler` icon of the entry directly above it.
- `organization-ownership-inventory.ts`, `platform-object-tenancy-census.json` — agree with each other and with the object (in reach, `organization_id`, attribution, no anchors).
- Integration test — real `SecurityPlugin` with the shipped sets, real object, real `AuditPlugin`, real caller resolution, `isolated` posture; the fixture-armed test asserts each persona's position, including that the administrator is not `org_member`. Refusals assert status, wire code and field, and that nothing was stored. Honest about its own limit: the posture it boots under is stated in the file and in the PR body.

No must-fix. S1 and S2 are owed, on this PR or a named follow-up, before the changeset is consumed by the release.

Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts + packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-standard-unit-setting.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-standard-unit-setting.object.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/system/index.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/plugin.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/setup-nav.contributions.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/default-permission-sets.standard-unit-setting.integration.test.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts, packages/cli/test/connect-agent-both-halves-wire.pin.test.ts, scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.json, .changeset/35498-standard-unit-setting.md (translation bundles spot-checked on the earlier head and untouched since)

### ① Derived judgments

This record is a fresh review of the new head. It rests on the whole-diff read made at `03e453e3d3076da4777dd5c288232b81561ce9a2` plus the delta from that head to this one (3 files, +38/−5: the changeset, the object's docblock, the integration test), the area's comment 7180963343, and the check-runs on this head. The delta changes no schema, no grant line, no registry name and no generated file, so every judgment below that the delta does not touch stands as read on the earlier head.

Check-runs on this head: every run is `success` or `skipped`, none failed or pending. `Test Core` (all ten shards), `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `Spec property liveness` are `success`. On the names that ran twice, `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` are `success` on the newer run; `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size` are `skipped` on the newer run.

- **`PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['platform-objects']` gains `sys_standard_unit_setting`** (the one `hits` path). Right: add-only, in sort order; the name becomes a reference target. A widening, nothing removed or re-meant. Unchanged by the delta.

Right against the `sys_unit.decimal_places` precedent and ADR-0158 L4. Unchanged by the delta (the object file's only hunk is the `Tenancy` docblock bullet).
- **`code` as text plus a format rule, not a select.** Right, declared (7179529249), pinned.
